dumbbell-inertia.alt: Two light rods each carry two equal masses m and turn about a vertical axis through their centers. In the top rod the masses sit a distance r from the axis, giving I = 2mr². In the bottom rod they sit at 2r, giving I = 8mr², four times as much with the same total mass. A panel gives I = Σmr², notes that doubling the distance quadruples I, and lists rotational inertias the exam gives for shapes: hoop MR², solid disk ½MR², solid sphere two fifths MR², rod about its center one twelfth ML², rod about one end one third ML². Unit kg·m².
